# WHELP-16 — assumptions

**Generated by `python -m bestiary.robots.whelp.provenance --md`. Do not hand-edit:**
`check.py` fails if this file differs from what that command writes, so an edit here
is reverted by the next regeneration and a stale edit is caught rather than trusted.

Every number the robot is built from appears below with its provenance. The five kinds,
and what each is worth, are documented at the top of `provenance.py`. The short version:

| kind | meaning | trust |
|---|---|---|
| `measured` | calipers or a scale on the actual object | highest — it is *this* unit |
| `primary` | datasheet, standard, paper, official source | high — but it is the nominal unit |
| `secondary` | a reputable project or reseller reproducing the number | medium |
| `choice` | a free design decision, made for a stated reason | n/a — not right or wrong |
| `assumed` | needed, unsourced | **lowest — each one names the measurement that retires it** |

> ⚠ **15 load-bearing assumptions** — these size a structural member, a
> torque margin, a joint limit or a clearance, and are *not* sourced. They are the
> shortlist of things to measure first, before printing anything expensive:
> `ground_friction`, `horn_bolt_circle_mm`, `horn_bolt_count`, `horn_bolt_dia_mm`, `horn_face_to_body_mm`, `print_bearing_strength_mpa`, `print_fatigue_knockdown`, `print_orientation_knockdown`, `print_shear_strength_mpa`, `servo_gear_break_multiple`, `servo_mount_hole_dx_mm`, `servo_mount_hole_dy_mm`, `servo_rear_boss_d_mm`, `tire_static_sag_mm`, `tire_stroke_mm`

## Assumed — unsourced, each with the measurement that would retire it

These are the robot's soft spots. `replaced_by` is not aspirational: it is a
list of experiments, most of which take under ten minutes with a scale, a
caliper, or a luggage scale and a lever arm.

| attribute | value | what it is | how to replace it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fastener_mass_kg` | `0.09` | All M3 hardware, inserts and bearings together. | massmodel.py counts them; weigh a bag of each to confirm |
| `ground_friction` ⚠ | `0.9` | TPU on a hard floor. | drag the powered-down robot on a luggage scale and read the breakaway force |
| `horn_bolt_circle_mm` ⚠ | `17` | Diameter of the circle the horn's screws sit on. THE interface torque leaves the servo through. | measure the horn with calipers, or print scad/parts/fitcheck.scad which carries five candidate circles on one 30-minute coupon |
| `horn_bolt_count` ⚠ | `4` | Number of screws in that circle. | count them on the horn in your hand |
| `horn_bolt_dia_mm` ⚠ | `2` | Their thread diameter. | measure one, or gauge it on the fit-check coupon |
| `horn_disc_d_mm` | `22` | Outer diameter of the metal horn disc. | calipers on the horn |
| `horn_face_to_body_mm` ⚠ | `3.5` | Horn face to case face, along the output axis. | calipers on the servo |
| `horn_hub_clear_d_mm` | `9` | Relief for the output boss and the horn's centre screw. | calipers on the servo |
| `horn_hub_clear_h_mm` | `4` | Depth of that relief. | calipers on the servo |
| `horn_thick_mm` | `2.5` | Horn thickness; sets the axial stack-up. | calipers on the horn |
| `print_bearing_strength_mpa` ⚠ | `45` | Bearing stress a bolt shank may apply to printed PETG before the hole ovals. Sets the horn boss thickness. | pull a single M3 through a printed lug on a luggage scale and record the load at first visible ovalling |
| `print_fatigue_knockdown` ⚠ | `0.42` | Fraction of static UTS a part may see at 1e6 cycles. 0.42 is measured for FDM PLA; a 2023 review found only ONE published fatigue study on PETG at all, so applying the PLA number to PETG is an extrapolation. | cycle one representative bracket to 1e5 cycles on a crank rig at the computed stance load; a weekend, and it is the number the whole structure is sized on |
| `print_orientation_knockdown` ⚠ | `0.85` | Allowance for print orientation never being perfectly aligned with the load path. | print the fit-check coupon's tensile bars in both orientations and take the ratio |
| `print_shear_strength_mpa` ⚠ | `28` | Shear strength across a printed web. Sets the sacrificial fuse's break load, which is the whole point of the fuse. | shear one printed fuse link in a vice against a luggage scale — ten minutes, and it is the single most valuable measurement on this list |
| `rolling_resistance` | `0.05` | Rolling resistance coefficient of a printed TPU tire. | roll the robot down a shallow ramp and find the angle at which it just keeps moving |
| `servo_cable_d_mm` | `5` | Harness bundle diameter at the servo. | calipers on the supplied cable |
| `servo_cable_inset_mm` | `6` | Cable exit position from the case end. | calipers on the servo |
| `servo_ear_span_l_mm` | `54` | Mounting flange span including the ears. | calipers on the servo case |
| `servo_ear_thick_mm` | `2.5` | Flange thickness. | calipers on the servo case |
| `servo_ear_z_from_body_mid_mm` | `10` | Flange height up the case from mid-body. | calipers on the servo case |
| `servo_gear_break_multiple` ⚠ | `1.8` | Gearbox failure torque as a multiple of stall. No manufacturer publishes it, and no citable teardown was found. It is the least-known number in the yield chain and the one that decides whether an overload is reversible. | sacrifice one servo: clamp the horn and load it to failure with a lever and a luggage scale. One servo and one afternoon buys the number the whole protection argument rests on |
| `servo_mount_hole_dx_mm` ⚠ | `38` | Case mounting hole pitch, lengthwise. No primary drawing was located: Feetech publishes torque, speed and current but no dimensioned print. | calipers on the servo case, or the fit-check coupon's mounting-pattern gauge |
| `servo_mount_hole_dy_mm` ⚠ | `18` | Case mounting hole pitch, across. | calipers on the servo case |
| `servo_mount_screw_mm` | `2.5` | Case mounting screw thread. | gauge one |
| `servo_output_boss_d_mm` | `12` | Diameter of the output boss under the horn. | calipers on the servo |
| `servo_rear_boss_d_mm` ⚠ | `6` | Diameter of that rear boss; the idler bearing rides on it. | calipers on the servo |
| `servo_rear_boss_h_mm` | `2` | Its height above the case. | calipers on the servo |
| `tire_static_sag_mm` ⚠ | `1.4` | Tire squash under the robot's own weight. Sets the LOADED radius, and building the URDF at the free radius spawns the robot into the floor. | stand the assembled robot on a flat surface and measure hub height with calipers; compare against the free radius |
| `tire_stroke_mm` ⚠ | `8` | Usable radial compression before the tire bottoms on the hub. Appears directly in torque.py's landing case, where it is most of the impact protection. | press a printed tire in a vice against a scale and record force against deflection to bottoming; twenty minutes, and it converts the whole impact budget from estimate to measurement |
| `wheel_damping` | `0.1` | Wheel viscous damping. | spin a wheel up and log its coast-down from the servo's own speed feedback; one command, ten seconds |
| `wheel_friction_nm` | `0.03` | Wheel Coulomb friction. | the same coast-down measurement gives both terms |
| `wiring_mass_kg` | `0.12` | Harness, connectors, bus splitters. | weigh the loom once it is built |

## Chosen — free design decisions

Nothing external validates these. They are judged only by whether the
requirements they exist to satisfy are met, which `check.py` tests.

| attribute | value | what it is | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `abduct_range_rad` ⚠ | `(-0.8, 0.8)` | From the brief. Wide enough to matter for a roll-over recovery, which Ascento's paper names as the failure that ends test sessions. | design decision |
| `abduct_to_hip_drop_mm` | `0` | Zero: keeps the abduction axis coplanar with the hip pivot so abduction torque has no vertical cross-term. | design decision |
| `abduct_to_hip_mm` ⚠ | `36` | Clears the abduction servo body plus the bracket wall. | design decision |
| `abduct_x_mm` ⚠ | `92` | Sets the 184 mm wheelbase. Longer resists wheelie better and turns worse. | design decision |
| `abduct_y_mm` ⚠ | `36` | WHERE the abduction pivot sits laterally, hence the track. Constrained inboard by the abduction servo fitting inside the trunk shell and outboard by the trunk's own side wall. Distinct from the abduction MOMENT ARM, which is how far the leg steps outboard of this pivot and is independent of it. | design decision |
| `battery_mass_kg` ⚠ | `0.2` | 3S 2200 mAh LiPo class. 16 servos at 0.9 A rated is 14.4 A, so this is a ~10 minute pack at full load. | design decision |
| `bed_x_mm` | `220` | Build volume from the brief. Every part is asserted to fit. | design decision |
| `bed_y_mm` | `220` | Build volume from the brief. | design decision |
| `bed_z_mm` | `240` | Assumed typical for a 220 mm bedslinger; not binding on any part here. | design decision |
| `calf_len_mm` ⚠ | `100` | From the brief. Shorter than the thigh so the stance solve has a solution across the whole hip range. | design decision |
| `calf_section_fore_aft_mm` ⚠ | `26` | As the thigh, shallower because the moment is lower. | design decision |
| `calf_section_lateral_mm` | `24` | Straddles the wheel drive. | design decision |
| `calf_to_wheel_plane_mm` ⚠ | `17` | Half the wheel width plus the calf wall plus clearance. It is also the abduction servo's moment arm. | design decision |
| `calf_wall_mm` ⚠ | `3.2` | As the thigh. | design decision |
| `compute_mass_kg` | `0.075` | Single-board computer plus the USB-to-TTL bus adapter. | design decision |
| `design_accel_m_s2` ⚠ | `0.5` | Forward acceleration the drive must produce. 0.5 m/s^2 reaches the machine's own 0.21 m/s top speed in 0.4 s, which is ample -- and it has to be modest, because the reflected rotor inertia makes the apparent mass for acceleration ~59 kg rather than 2.2. See torque.wheel_budget. | design decision |
| `design_drop_height_mm` ⚠ | `8` | The free-fall drop the leg is designed to survive inside its margin. 20 mm is small, and it is what the tire's stroke supports -- see torque.py, which derives it rather than assuming it. | design decision |
| `design_slope_deg` | `20` | Slope the wheel drive must climb. | design decision |
| `fuse_enable` ⚠ | `True` | Fitted by default: two grams and two minutes of print time to make the cheapest item in the yield chain a part swap. | design decision |
| `fuse_shear_area_mm2` ⚠ | `10` | Sized so the fuse shears below the servo gearbox's estimated strength and below the calf's. torque.py checks the order. | design decision |
| `fuse_thick_mm` | `2` | Web thickness; with the area it sets the break load. | design decision |
| `hip_range_rad` ⚠ | `(-1.2, 2.6)` | From the brief. | design decision |
| `horn_boss_thick_mm` ⚠ | `5` | Plastic thickness the horn screws bear against. Torque arrives as a force on each screw shank bearing against printed plastic, so this times the bolt diameter is the bearing area. Thin bosses do not shear the screws -- steel wins -- they oval out, and the joint develops the backlash the double-shear pivot was fitted to prevent. | design decision |
| `idler_bearing_shelf_mm` | `1.2` | Shoulder that stops the outer race at a known depth. | design decision |
| `knee_range_rad` ⚠ | `(-2.6, -0.6)` | From the brief. One-sided, so the knee only ever folds one way. | design decision |
| `layer_mm` | `0.2` | 0.2 mm. The literature contradicts itself on layer height, so this is held constant across the robot for comparability rather than optimised. | design decision |
| `material` ⚠ | `PETG` | PETG. PLA and Tough PLA are disqualified by heat: their HDT at 0.45 MPa is 55 degC and a bracket bolted to a servo that has been holding torque sits at 50-70 degC. ASA and PETG-CF are better still (HDT 93 and 96) and swap in by changing this and the three material numbers below. | design decision |
| `name` | `whelp16` | Callsign. A whelp is a young hound, and this is hound's hardware sibling. | design decision |
| `nozzle_mm` | `0.4` | 0.4 mm. A 0.6 mm nozzle is stronger and faster and would change every wall thickness here, so it is a spec change and not a slicer setting. | design decision |
| `required_torque_margin` ⚠ | `2` | 2x, from the brief. Applied against RATED torque for sustained poses and against STALL for transients. | design decision |
| `scad_fn` | `64` | Facets per circle in the CAD. Preview uses fewer; export uses this. | design decision |
| `servo_cable_stub_mm` | `18` | Straight run reserved before the harness may bend. A serial bus servo has a cable at BOTH ends, and a leg that pinches one takes the whole bus down, not one joint. | design decision |
| `servo_torque_limit_frac` ⚠ | `0.5` | Written to the Torque Limit register at boot. Caps SLOW overload only -- leaning, pushing, standing wrong. It does nothing for a landing, because the reflected rotor inertia makes the joint rigid on impact timescales. | design decision |
| `stance_abduct_rad` | `0` | Legs vertical in the frontal plane. Widening buys roll stability and costs abduction torque all day. | design decision |
| `stance_hip_rad` ⚠ | `0.46` | Chosen against the knee lever arm, which is L_thigh*sin(hip). 0.55 rad gives a 57 mm lever at 84% leg extension -- the knee of the trade between torque and remaining travel. See the table in the class body. | design decision |
| `thigh_len_mm` ⚠ | `110` | From the brief. Its sine at the stance angle IS the knee's lever arm, so it sets the actuator budget. | design decision |
| `thigh_section_fore_aft_mm` ⚠ | `30` | Channel depth in the bending plane; stiffness goes as its cube. | design decision |
| `thigh_section_lateral_mm` | `32` | Wide enough to straddle the servo in double shear. | design decision |
| `thigh_wall_mm` ⚠ | `3.2` | Six perimeters at 0.4 mm plus a margin for the fillet root. | design decision |
| `tire_infill_frac` | `0.25` | Gyroid at 25%. Lower is softer and takes a set faster. | design decision |
| `tire_thickness_mm` ⚠ | `12` | Radial TPU section. It is the only mechanical compliance in the leg, so it is a structural number. | design decision |
| `trunk_height_mm` | `58` | Battery plus a single-board computer, stacked. | design decision |
| `trunk_len_mm` ⚠ | `250` | From the brief. Also sets the wheelbase and so the wheelie limit. | design decision |
| `trunk_split_lap_mm` ⚠ | `26` | 250 mm does not fit a 220 mm bed, so the trunk splits at the midplane. A lap joint this long carries the load in shear across a large area instead of in tension across a butt line. | design decision |
| `trunk_wall_mm` ⚠ | `2.4` | Six perimeters at a 0.4 mm nozzle. Walls carry a printed box, not infill: 1->3 perimeters measured +51% tensile while 40->100% infill dropped specific strength 38%. | design decision |
| `trunk_width_mm` | `104` | Wide enough for a 3S pack between the abduction brackets. | design decision |
| `wheel_drive_kind` ⚠ | `sts3215_c018` | Same part as the legs in v1: one SKU, one 12 V bus, no extra drivers. Also the slowest option available, by roughly six times. | design decision |
| `wheel_drive_part` | `sts3215` | Same servo as the legs in v1. | design decision |
| `wheel_radius_mm` ⚠ | `45` | From the brief. Directly sets top speed at a given motor rpm. | design decision |
| `wheel_upgrade_max_mass_kg` | `0.06` | At or below the servo it replaces, so the leg's distal inertia does not get worse. | design decision |
| `wheel_upgrade_min_nm` | `0.2` | Above the 20 deg slope demand with margin, and well under the friction-cone ceiling torque.py computes. | design decision |
| `wheel_width_mm` | `24` | Contact patch and lateral stability against a tipping moment. | design decision |
| `yield_knee_rad` ⚠ | `0.35` | Knee rotation the design is willing to spend absorbing a SLOW overload before something else has to stop it. | design decision |

Believable, but an upstream transcription error would be invisible here.
Worth promoting to `measured` when the part is in hand.

| attribute | value | what it is | source |

| `insert_mass_kg` | `0.0009` | ~0.9 g each, and there are dozens. Concentrated at joints, which is where inertia matters most. | Ruthex M3 x 5.7, brass |
| `insert_wall_mm` ⚠ | `1.8` | Material around the insert boss. | Ruthex minimum wall guidance (1.6 mm), rounded up |
| `joint_damping` | `0.56` | Identified viscous damping, N.m/(rad/s). | Open Duck Mini v2 MJCF, STS3215 parameters identified with Rhoban BAM |
| `joint_friction_nm` | `0.068` | Identified Coulomb friction. | Open Duck Mini v2 MJCF, STS3215 parameters identified with Rhoban BAM |
| `leg_servo_rated_nm` ⚠ | `0.980665` | 'Rated load: 10kg.cm'. THE number a sustained-pose budget uses: a 3x derate from stall. Feetech's own page does not publish a rated load for C018. | https://www.dfrobot.com/product-2962.html<br>*disagrees with:* Feetech C001 (7.4 V) page states 6.5 kgf.cm rated at 6 V; Seeed states 5 kgf.cm; DFRobot states 4 kgf.cm — three sources, three numbers, for the sibling variant |
| `print_effective_solid_frac` ⚠ | `0.5` | Fraction of CAD solid volume that is actually plastic. NOT the infill fraction: on a part whose smallest dimension is under ~20 mm the walls are most of the volume. | worked example: 5 walls at 0.4 mm on a 110 x 25 x 18 mm part, 25% gyroid |
| `servo_armature_kgm2` ⚠ | `0.027` | Reflected rotor inertia at the joint, identified with Rhoban BAM on this exact servo. ~100x the thigh's own inertia. Omitting it makes the simulated leg a massless whip. | Open Duck Mini v2 MJCF, STS3215 parameters identified with Rhoban BAM |
| `servo_backlash_rad` ⚠ | `0.0151844` | 0.87 deg measured, against a 0.5 deg published maximum. With the deadband it is ~1.75 deg of total dead motion, which is a floor on how finely any policy can act. | Open Duck Mini v2 MJCF, STS3215 parameters identified with Rhoban BAM |
| `servo_deadband_counts` | `1` | Register default is 1 step = 0.088 deg. | FEETECH SCServo SDK control table, registers 26/27 (CW/CCW dead zone)<br>*disagrees with:* an independent bench report describes a ~10-count (0.88 deg) effective dead zone, 10x the register default — measure yours |
| `servo_rated_current_a` | `0.9` | 0.9 A at rated load. Sixteen is 14.4 A continuous, which sizes the pack and the wiring. | https://www.dfrobot.com/product-2962.html |
| `wheel_drive_rated_nm` | `0.980665` | As the leg servo. | https://www.dfrobot.com/product-2962.html |
| `wheel_upgrade_min_rpm` | `300` | 300 rpm on a 45 mm wheel is 1.41 m/s, the envelope a 250 mm machine supports. | Froude scaling from Unitree Go2-W (Fr = 0.954) and B2-W (Fr = 1.27) to a 0.25 m body |

## Primary — datasheet, standard, paper, or official source

Trustworthy for the *nominal* part. The unit on your bench may differ, which
is why some of these are still worth re-measuring.

| attribute | value | what it is | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bearing_press_fit_mm` ⚠ | `-0.2` | 0.2 mm diametral interference. Measured to need ~585 N to press into PETG, which is firm by hand with an arbor press and does not fall out. | CNC Kitchen, instrumented heat-set insert and press-fit test series |
| `fillet_r_mm` ⚠ | `3` | Radius on EVERY internal corner. A 0.3 mm as-modelled corner gives Kt = 2.99 in bending; 3 mm gives 1.48. Halving peak stress for zero mass and zero print time is the cheapest strength in the design. | Pilkey, Peterson's Stress Concentration Factors, filleted flat bar |
| `idler_bearing_id_mm` | `3` | 623ZZ bore. | ISO 15 / bearing catalogue, 623ZZ metric miniature series |
| `idler_bearing_od_mm` | `10` | 623ZZ outer diameter. | ISO 15 / bearing catalogue, 623ZZ metric miniature series |
| `idler_bearing_w_mm` | `4` | 623ZZ width. | ISO 15 / bearing catalogue, 623ZZ metric miniature series |
| `insert_bore_mm` ⚠ | `4.2` | 4.2 mm for a vertical M3 x 5.7 insert. Too tight splits the boss; too loose spins the insert on first torque. | CNC Kitchen, instrumented heat-set insert and press-fit test series |
| `insert_len_mm` | `5.7` | 5.7 mm. | Ruthex M3 x 5.7 product data |
| `insert_od_mm` | `4.6` | 4.6 mm outer diameter. | Ruthex M3 x 5.7 product data |
| `insert_pullout_n` | `1167` | 119 kgf in PETG. Comparable to a direct screw, but the insert survives repeated assembly and the screw does not. | CNC Kitchen, instrumented heat-set insert and press-fit test series |
| `insert_torque_fail_nm` ⚠ | `3` | 3 N.m in PETG, the best of every method tested (direct screw 1, helicoil 1, captive nut 2). It also sits above every joint torque in this design, which is what makes the fastener not the weak link. | CNC Kitchen, instrumented heat-set insert and press-fit test series |
| `leg_servo_gear_ratio` ⚠ | `345` | 1:345. The reason the joint is effectively rigid on impact timescales. | https://www.feetechrc.com/525603.html |
| `leg_servo_no_load_rad_s` ⚠ | `4.71239` | 'No load speed: 0.222sec/60 deg @12V' = 45 rpm = 4.712 rad/s. Under load it is less. About a sixth of the 30 rad/s every published legged-RL config assumes. | https://www.feetechrc.com/525603.html |
| `leg_servo_stall_nm` ⚠ | `2.94199` | 'Peak stall torque: 30kg.cm@12V'. MOMENTARY -- the word peak is Feetech's. Used for transient cases only. | https://www.feetechrc.com/525603.html |

| `m3_nut_thick_mm` | `2.4` | M3 nut thickness. | ISO 4032 |

| `print_infill_frac` | `0.25` | 25% gyroid. Going 0 -> 100% infill raised absolute strength 32% but dropped strength PER KILOGRAM by 38%, which on a mass-budgeted robot is the wrong direction. | Polymers 14(12) 2446 — specific strength vs infill for PET-G |
| `print_kt` ⚠ | `1.48` | Stress concentration at a filleted internal corner, evaluated for a representative 20/14 mm step with a 3 mm radius. | Pilkey, Peterson's Stress Concentration Factors, filleted flat bar |

⚠ marks a **load-bearing** number: one that sizes a structural member, a torque margin, a
joint limit or a clearance. Being wrong about an unmarked number looks odd; being wrong
about a marked one breaks hardware.
